title: A checkpoint or a harder written answer
statement: Whether an independent turn may drop a step's tap-to-choose checkpoint for a harder written answer, losing the step's label and practice rejecting options that don't fit, is unsettled.
example: The design's bank offered 9 words to lock in or bounce back, where the free-typed version accepted any of 4 typed words.
detail: A simulated review of a reading lesson found an independent-practice step with no gate and no printed label, its knowledge move carried instead by two assessed blanks in the next step's written frame (`grade3-reading/artifacts/arc-audit/REGISTER-2026-09-15.md`, lines 37-43). The prepared answer defends free writing because the independent turn should ask more of the child than the guided turn, which already offers the tapping version of the same move (line 43). An earlier audit judged a free-typed version of the step higher in demand, recall rather than recognition, but found it drops the design's practice in rejecting words that don't fit (`grade3-reading/artifacts/arc-audit/PEDAGOGY-L5-2026-09-05.md`, lines 247-256). The register held three paths for a ruling, and a later register still listed the step among gaps awaiting rulings, with nothing executed (`grade3-reading/artifacts/arc-audit/REGISTER-2026-09-24.md`, lines 25-26).
against: The register leaned toward restoring the step: "path A recommended: gated Step 3 question, p17 becomes a stepped rail like L2/L4" (`grade3-reading/artifacts/arc-audit/REGISTER-2026-09-15.md`, line 187). The earlier audit's free-typed hunt sits in notes that only a retired player draws (the same register, line 40), though its point about the lost rejection holds for the written fold as well.

evidence.quote: We chose free writing over tapping at this point because the independent turn should ask more of the child than the guided turn did, and the guided turn on the previous screen already offers the tapping version of the same move.

do we add a gated Step-3 msq and accept that p17 flips into a staged Routine while p16 stays a plain stack, add it unlabelled to keep both pages in the same mode, or rule that folding add-what-you-know into Step 4's assessed know-a/know-b blanks is the intended fade?

The JSON's free-type version is arguably higher cognitive demand (recall vs. recognition) but is a different interaction shape than the doc specifies, and it drops the "don't fit" distractor-rejection teaching moment the doc's bank interaction provides
